english: Let $E$ be the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{75}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{25}=1$ and let $H$ be the hyperbola $\dfrac{(x-20)^{2}}{196}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{16}=1$. Let $A$ and $B$ be the two points in the plane from each of which the two tangents drawn to $E$ are perpendicular to each other and the two tangents drawn to $H$ are also perpendicular to each other. If $O$ and $C$ are the centres of $E$ and $H$ respectively, then the area of the quadrilateral $OACB$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $E$ दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{75}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{25}=1$ है तथा $H$ अतिपरवलय $\dfrac{(x-20)^{2}}{196}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{16}=1$ है। माना कि $A$ तथा $B$ समतल के वे दो बिन्दु हैं जिनमें से प्रत्येक से $E$ पर खींची गई दोनों स्पर्श रेखाएँ परस्पर लम्बवत हैं तथा $H$ पर खींची गई दोनों स्पर्श रेखाएँ भी परस्पर लम्बवत हैं। यदि $O$ तथा $C$ क्रमशः $E$ तथा $H$ के केन्द्र हैं, तो चतुर्भुज $OACB$ का क्षेत्रफल ______ है।
solution: $A,B$ are the common points: subtracting, $40x-400=-80\Rightarrow x=8$, $y^{2}=100-64=36\Rightarrow A(8,6),\ B(8,-6)$
$OACB$ is a kite with diagonals $OC=20$ (on the $x$-axis) and $AB=12$, perpendicular to each other
solution_full: For the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ the locus of points from which the tangents are perpendicular is the director circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}$. For $E$: $x^{2}+y^{2}=75+25=100$, centre $O(0,0)$, radius $10$.

For the hyperbola $\dfrac{X^{2}}{a^{2}}-\dfrac{Y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ (with $a>b$) the director circle is $X^{2}+Y^{2}=a^{2}-b^{2}$. For $H$, with $X=x-20,\ Y=y$: $(x-20)^{2}+y^{2}=196-16=180$, centre $C(20,0)$, radius $\sqrt{180}$.
A point from which both pairs of tangents are perpendicular lies on both circles. Subtracting the equations: $x^{2}-(x-20)^{2}=100-180$, i.e. $40x-400=-80$, so $x=8$.
Then $y^{2}=100-64=36$, so $y=\pm 6$. Hence $A(8,6)$ and $B(8,-6)$. The circles meet in exactly these two points.

Check for $A(8,6)$ and $H$: a line $y-6=m(x-8)$ touches $H$ when $(6+12m)^{2}=196m^{2}-16$, i.e. $52m^{2}-144m-52=0$; the product of the roots is $-1$ and both roots satisfy $196m^{2}-16>0$, so the two tangents exist and are perpendicular. The same holds for $E$ ($11m^{2}+96m-11=0$).

In $OACB$, the diagonal $OC$ lies on the $x$-axis with length $20$ and the diagonal $AB$ is the vertical segment $x=8,\ -6\le y\le 6$ of length $12$. The diagonals are perpendicular, and $AB$ meets $OC$ at $(8,0)$, between $O$ and $C$, so $OACB$ is a convex kite.

concept_use.Director circle for Hyperbola: Perpendicular tangents to H come from points of its director circle (x-20)^2+y^2=196-16=180.
concept_use.Director circle for Ellipse: Perpendicular tangents to E come from points of its director circle x^2+y^2=75+25=100; A and B are the common points of the two circles.

originality_note: New: the points are defined by a double orthoptic condition (perpendicular tangents to an ellipse and to a shifted hyperbola at once), so they are the common points of two director circles; the area of the kite they form with the two centres is then read off (way 3). Closest known: equation of the director circle of an ellipse or of a hyperbola. Different because: the two loci must be intersected, and the hyperbola is shifted so the circles are not concentric.
stem_review: Read as a student: every curve, point and parameter introduced, conditions complete (quadrant / sign / branch stated), one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer equals the plan (positive 3-digit integer: 120). Changed: No change. Checked that the director circles meet in exactly two points, that from each point both pairs of tangents are real (slopes satisfy 196m^2-16>0), and that OACB is convex.
key_step: Recognise both conditions as director circles and intersect the two non-concentric circles.
justification: Two ideas linked: director circles of an ellipse and of a shifted hyperbola, then their intersection and an area; numerical format with no options. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q13 (L3), an ellipse-hyperbola numerical combining standard elements.
